_note: Saadia-specific JA→EN gloss patterns, extracted from the Bereshit 1 English draft (data/tafsir-bereshit-1-english.json) and Blau's Genesis study (data-source/blau-genesis-notes.json). The English in the Tafsir reader is meant to enable reverse-translation: a reader looks at the JA and uses the English to disambiguate it. So this table records Saadia's *interpretive moves*, not generic Arabic vocabulary — those moves are where translation choice matters and where Saadia's JA diverges from the Hebrew or from Lane's classical Arabic. Where Saadia's JA sense differs from Lane, follow Blau (Dictionary of Medieval Judaeo-Arabic Texts).
_source: data/tafsir-bereshit-1-english.json (manually-drafted exemplar; treat as authoritative voice)
data-source/blau-genesis-notes.json (Yehoshua Blau, Studies in Saadia Gaon's Translation of Genesis ch.1-12)
principles: Translate the Judeo-Arabic, NOT the biblical Hebrew. Where Saadia interprets, his interpretation is part of the source text.
Preserve Saadia's signature substitutions verbatim: שא→'willed', עלם→'knew', ריאח (pl.)→'winds', פכאן→'and so it was', צורה→'form' (for צלם), נפסא נאטקה→'a rational soul'.
Reverse-translatability: a careful reader should be able to map most English words back to a JA word in the same verse. Don't smooth toward the biblical Hebrew.
When Saadia's JA usage differs from Lane's classical sense (e.g. גלד = 'firmament' not 'ice'; אד = 'when/since' not 'if/lo'; שא = 'willed' not just 'wished'), follow Blau's gloss.
Saadia rationalizes anthropomorphisms — ויאמר → 'willed that' (שא), וירא → 'knew' (עלם), בצלם → 'in [His] form' (בצורתה). Keep these.
Hendiadys patterns: 'הלוך וX' → 'each time ... [Xed more]' (per Blau 8:3, 8:5); not literal 'going and X-ing'.

Saadia identifies place-names: פישון = Nile (אלניל), חוילה = Zawila, כוש = Abyssinia (אלחבשה), אשור = Mosul (אלמוצל), חידקל = Tigris (אלדגלה). Use Saadia's identification in the English with the biblical name in brackets only if needed for legibility.
Saadia's pithy ערב-בקר rendering: 'וַלַמּא מצ'י' מן אלליל ואלנהאר יום N' → 'And there passed of night and daytime an Nth day' (Blau 1:5).
Saadia uses 'סאיר' (the rest of) for second 'כל' in a verse to avoid repetition (Blau 1:21). Render as 'and the rest of' or 'and every other'.
Saadia softens 'מות תמות' → 'תסתחק אן תמות' = 'you shall deserve to die' (Blau 2:17). Render literally as Saadia gives it.
Saadia uses 'אדם' as a proper noun throughout (treat as 'Adam' not 'man' from Gen 2:7 onward — same as Hebrew translation's 'אדם הראשון').

For waw-consecutive openers Saadia commonly elides: render 'פצנע / פכ'לק / פסמי' / פבארך' as 'And [God] made / created / called / blessed' (don't add 'then' unless the Arabic has ת'ם, in which case 'then' or 'and then').

entries.note: Saadia's signature substitute for the divine speech-jussive. Always followed by 'אן יכון X' = 'that there be X'.
Complement of שא. With plural: 'אן תכון' = 'that there be [pl.]'.

entries.en: and there was / and so it was
entries.note: Saadia's tight rendering of ויהי. With כד'אך: 'פכאן כד'אך' = 'and so it was'.
Saadia's signature replacement for 'and [God] saw' — rationalizes the anthropomorphism. NOT 'saw'.
Saadia pluralizes 'ruach' — keep plural in English.
Saadia's interpretive rendering of tohu-vavohu — describes the watery primeval state.

entries.en: the face of the water / the face of the deep

entries.note: Blau-vs-Lane: Lane has גלד = 'hard, frozen'. Saadia's JA sense is the firmament/expanse of the sky — follow Blau.
Saadia condenses the doubled 'מים למים' to a dual.

entries.en: which is below it ... which is above it
the times of light / the times of darkness
entries.note: Saadia's rationalizing insertion: God doesn't call light 'day' literally — He calls the *times* of light 'day'.

entries.ja: וַלַמּא מצ'י' מן אלליל ואלנהאר יום N
entries.ar: ولما مضى من الليل والنهار يوم N
entries.he_source: ויהי ערב ויהי בקר יום N
entries.en: And there passed of night and daytime an Nth day
entries.note: Saadia's signature pithy rendering — keep this exact English phrasing for every evening-morning verse. The numerals: 'ואחד' = first/one, 'ת'אני' = second, 'ת'אלת'' = third, 'ראבע' = fourth, 'כ'אמס' = fifth, 'סאדס' = sixth, 'סאבע' = seventh.
Per Blau 1:9, Petersburg MS has plural 'תג'תמע אלאמיא'; printed is singular. Use singular 'water' as Kapach gives it.

entries.en: according to its kinds / its kinds
entries.note: Saadia uses PLURAL 'kinds' (אצנאף) where Hebrew has singular מין — preserve plural.

entries.en: the greater luminary / the lesser luminary

entries.note: Saadia substitutes 'giving light' for the Hebrew 'ממשלת' (rulership) — rationalizing.

entries.en: moving creature possessing a living soul
facing the firmament of the sky
and the rest of / and every other
entries.note: Blau 1:21: Saadia uses סאיר for the second 'כל' to avoid repetition. Pattern recurs at 6:20, 7:21, etc.

entries.en: And God blessed them / the two of them

entries.note: Saadia's signature interpretive layer on 'לאמר' — frames the speech as a decree.

entries.en: creeping thing / creeping thing of the earth / that creeps

entries.note: In Gen 1:26 Saadia has 'אנסאן' (humankind, collective). From Gen 2:7 onward Saadia uses 'אדם' as a proper noun = 'Adam'.
Saadia's interpretive substitution — צורה for צלם. Avoids 'image' / anthropomorphism.
Saadia's signature insertion in Gen 1:26-27 — frames the divine 'image' as sovereignty/rulership over creation, an anti-anthropomorphic gloss.
Saadia uses the military sense — 'armies/hosts' of the heavens.

entries.en: He desisted / and He desisted from
entries.note: Saadia's rationalizing substitute for 'rested' — avoids the anthropomorphism. 'עטל אן' = 'desisted from doing'.

entries.en: from the like of His creation that He had made
entries.note: Per Blau 2:3: Kapach reads 'מעין בריאה' (no possessive) but Blau argues for 'מעין בריאתו' (possessive). The Cairo printing has the possessive form 'כ'לקה' — render as 'His creation'.
Saadia interpretively renders 'תולדות' (generations / story) as 'exposition of the originating events'.
Saadia renders 'יום' here as 'time/period' not literal 'day' — rationalizing.
Saadia takes 'שדה' as the open wilderness/desert, not cultivated field.

entries.ja: קבל אן יכון / קבל אן ינבת
entries.ar: قبل أن يكون / قبل أن ينبت
entries.en: before it was / before it grew
entries.note: Blau 2:5: Saadia recognizes טרם can mark 'before' (temporal) or 'still not' (descriptive). Here, the verse-context calls for the temporal 'before'.

entries.en: and there was no human to till it

entries.note: Blau 2:6: Kapach has 'מן האדמה'; Blau argues for 'ממנה' (= 'from it', referring back to הארץ). Cairo follows Blau here.
Blau 2:7 prefers reading with explicit 'אז' (then) sequencing — Kapach struck it. Cairo's reading without 'אז' is followed here; render as a simple narrative 'God created Adam'.

entries.en: a rational soul / a speaking soul
entries.note: Saadia's signature philosophical move — renders 'living soul' as 'rational/speaking soul' (the soul defined by speech-reason). Cf. Hebrew translation 'נֶפֶשׁ דוֹבֶרֶת'. Keep 'rational soul' as English.

entries.en: in Eden, easterly / in eastern Eden
fair of appearance and good for eating
the tree of the knowledge of good and evil

entries.note: Saadia identifies Pishon with the Nile. Render as 'the Nile (Pishon)' on first occurrence in a chapter; thereafter just 'the Nile'.
Blau 2:11: Saadia identifies Havilah with Zawila — a Maghreb gold-trading center known to Arabic geographers. On first occurrence give as 'Zawila (Havilah)'.
Saadia identifies Cush with Abyssinia. Give as 'Abyssinia (Cush)' on first occurrence.
Saadia identifies Asshur with Mosul — the chief Iraqi city near the Tigris in his day. Give as 'Mosul (Asshur)' on first occurrence.

entries.en: and settled him in the garden of Eden
to till it and to guard it
it is permitted that you eat
entries.note: Saadia softens the absolute infinitive 'אכל תאכל' — renders as a permission ('it is permitted') rather than emphatic 'surely eat'.
Blau 2:17: Saadia softens 'mot tamut' to 'you shall be liable to death' / 'you shall deserve to die'. Keep the softer English.

entries.ja: לא כ'יר פי בקא אדם וחדה
entries.ar: لا خير في بقاء آدم وحده
entries.en: there is no good in Adam's remaining alone
entries.note: Blau 2:18: Saadia uses 'בקא' (= 'remain') rather than literal 'היות' (= 'be'). Render with 'remaining'.

entries.en: a helper facing him / a counterpart helper

entries.note: Blau 2:19: at this point Saadia does NOT use 'created' (he already created the animals in Gen 1) — he uses 'חשר' = gathered/mustered. Petersburg MS has 'אסף האל' = 'and God gathered'; Kapach has 'פחשר'. Cairo follows Kapach. Render as 'gathered' or 'mustered'.

entries.en: to show him [what he would name them]
entries.note: Blau 2:19: Saadia renders 'לראות' as the CAUSATIVE 'להראותו' (= 'to show *him*', i.e. Adam). Translate as 'to show him', not 'to see'.

entries.ja: לם יגד לנפסה / לם יוגד לאדם
entries.en: did not find for himself / no helper was found for Adam
entries.note: Blau 2:20: prefers Petersburg's 'ולם יוגד לאדם עון' (impersonal passive: 'no helper was found for Adam'); Kapach has 'ולם יגד אדם עונא' (active: 'Adam did not find a helper'). Cairo follows Kapach here ('לם יגד לנפסה' = 'did not find for himself'). Render 'did not find for himself'.

entries.en: And God caused a deep sleep to fall
so that he should not feel [it]
entries.note: Saadia's interpretive insertion — explains WHY the deep sleep ('so he wouldn't feel the rib being taken'). Keep the insertion.

entries.en: He extracted one of his ribs
and closed up its place with flesh
He built from it a woman
this time I have seen bone
entries.note: Blau 2:23: Saadia uses 'שאהדת' (= 'I have seen / witnessed'), not literal 'מצאתי'. Render as 'I have seen' / 'I have witnessed'.

entries.en: it is fitting that she be called woman
entries.note: Blau 2:23: Saadia uses 'ינבגי' (= 'it is fit/proper'). Render as 'fitting'.
Blau 2:24 notes Petersburg vs. Derenbourg variation here. Cairo gives 'גסמא ואחדא' = 'a single body'. Render as 'a single body' rather than 'one flesh'.

entries.en: and they did not feel shame

entries.note: Blau 3:1: Saadia translates 'אף כי' as 'indeed' / 'verily'. Render with the appropriate emphatic adverb in English.
Blau 3:3: 'דנא ב' is a rare Aramaic-influenced idiom (rather than classical 'קרב אל' or 'מסה'). Render as 'approach' to preserve the cautious tone.

entries.en: as the day was moving / at the cooling movement of the day
entries.note: Blau 3:8 confirms Kapach's 'כתנועת היום' — Saadia takes 'רוח היום' as the movement/turn of the day (toward evening).

Blau 3:16-17: Saadia renders 'עצב/עצבון' (lit. 'pain / sadness') as 'effort/toil' (משקה) or 'fatigue/labor' (יגיעה). Kapach's distinction between 'בצער' and 'ביגע' is unsupported. Render consistently as 'toil' or 'labor'.
Blau 3:22: Saadia translates 'לעולם' as 'forever' (אלי אלדהר). Kapach's note suggesting 'a generation/דור' is unjustified — render as 'forever'.
Disambiguate by context: locative 'ת'ם' = there; sequential 'ת'ם קאל' = 'then said'.

entries.en: I am at your service / here I am
entries.note: Saadia renders הנני with the Islamic-flavored 'labbayk' formula. Render as 'I am at your service' (or 'here I am') — keeps the deferential force.
Saadia uses אמתחן for divine testing. Distinct from generic 'נסה'.

entries.en: [the land of] worship / the land of worship
entries.note: Saadia interprets מוריה (Moriah) as 'place of worship' — renames the Akedah site by its function.
Saadia's universal term for sacrificial offering — used for both עולה and קרבן. Don't switch to 'burnt offering' unless the JA specifies a burnt sacrifice.

entries.en: youth / his two youths / the youths
entries.note: Saadia's standard word for נער (vs. literal צבי or וליד). The dual form ג'לאמיה = 'his two youths'.
Saadia uses אדלג (depart at dawn) for וישכם — captures the pre-dawn departure precisely.
Saadia's standard rendering of המקום. Generic locative — don't add 'holy' unless context demands.

entries.en: the land / the country / the town
entries.note: Saadia uses בלד for both 'land' (= ארץ) AND 'town/city' (= עיר). Disambiguate by context: 'בלד כנעאן' = 'land of Canaan'; 'אהל אלבלד' = 'people of the town/city'; 'באב אלבלד' = 'gate of the town'.

entries.en: the people of the town / the people of

entries.note: Saadia uses אלקום (the clan/group) for עם in narrative settings. Distinct from אלאמה (the nation).
Saadia's word for political/genealogical nation (vs. אלקום for a clan).

entries.en: the people of / the family of

entries.he_source: ויהי כ- / ויהי כאשר / ויהי כי
entries.en: and when / and it was when / when [time-marker] was
entries.note: Saadia's standard narrative opener for ויהי-followed-by-time-clause. 'פלמא כאן בעד הד'ה אלאמור' = 'and it was after these things'.
entries.source: B22 v.1; B41 v.1; B12 v.11; passim

entries.note: Saadia renders 'והנה' (presentative) as 'פאד'א'. Keep 'behold' or 'and there [was/were]'.
Saadia's discourse particle for גם.
Saadia's narrative 'then-clause' marker. Distinct from ת'ם (next-in-sequence).
Saadia's standard for ועתה — a discourse-resumptive 'and now' that recommends/commands action.
Per Blau: Saadia uses אד' for both 'since/when' (temporal/causal) and 'if' (conditional). Disambiguate by context.

entries.en: beautiful in appearance / fair of appearance
ugly in appearance / of evil appearance
stout of flesh / fat of flesh
lean of flesh / thin of flesh

entries.note: Saadia identifies the biblical רוח קדים (east wind) with the 'qibla wind' — the wind from the direction of qibla (south in Babylon/Mesopotamia). Render literally as 'qibla-wind' or 'south wind' — NOT 'east wind'.

entries.en: his spirit was troubled / his soul was wrung

entries.note: Saadia avoids the foreign-sounding 'חרטם' (Egyptian magician); renders as 'learned men' / 'sages'.
Proper-name transliteration — keep as 'Israel' in English.
Saadia uses פצ'ה for silver as commodity (vs. כסף which in JA can mean 'money' generally — Saadia disambiguates).
Saadia uses זוגה (consort) for אשה. Distinct from אמראה (woman, as a general category).
Saadia uses אמראה for 'woman' generically (not specifically 'wife'). For 'wife', use זוגה.

entries.ja: בין ידי / בין ידיה / בין ידי אללה
entries.ar: بين يدي / بين يديه / بين يدي الله
entries.en: before / before him / before God / in [God's] presence
entries.note: Saadia's standard rendering of לפני. 'בין ידי אללה' = 'before God / in God's presence'.
Saadia's wordplay on יצחק's name. Saadia preserves the etymological pun where context permits.
Saadia uses כ'אדם (servant/official) for סריס — avoids the literal 'eunuch' and reframes as a court official.
Saadia preserves the etymological gloss on Edom (= the red one). Render as 'the Red One (Edom)' on first occurrence, then either 'the Red One' or 'Edomites' as plural.
Saadia avoids 'prince' (literal נשיא); uses Arabic socio-political term שריף for tribal eminence.
Saadia softens תם ('whole/perfect') to סאדגא (Persian-derived 'simple/innocent'). Render with 'simple' or 'innocent'.

entries.en: the imām / the imām of Midian
entries.note: For NON-ISRAELITE priests (Jethro of Midian, Potiphera in Egypt), Saadia uses אמאם (= imām / leader / community-head) rather than the cultic 'priest'. This is a deliberate move — avoids attributing legitimate priestly authority to gentile cult-officials while respecting their social role. For Aaronic/Levitical priests, Saadia uses different terms (verify context-by-context).
Saadia uses תאבות (tābūt — same word as the Ark of the Covenant) both for Noah's ark and for the basket-ark of Moses. Render 'an ark' to preserve the connection.
Saadia preserves the Egyptian-derived term for the bulrush from which Moses' ark was made.
Saadia's word for the rushes where Moses' ark was set. Distinct from בחר אלקלזם (Saadia's Red Sea = Sea of Suf).
Saadia's word for the infant/young child. Use 'babe' for infants (Moses in basket), 'boy' for older children (the crying naar at Hagar's well in B21 was 'youth').
Saadia avoids the moral-religious term 'wicked' (which would be אלכאפר or similar) and uses אלצ'אלם — 'the one doing wrong/oppressive act' in the situational sense.
Saadia smooths the Hebrew duplication 'כה וכה' (this-way and that-way) to the literal 'right and left'.

entries.en: the name of one ... and the other / and the second

entries.note: Saadia's interpretation of the obscure 'האבנים' (lit. 'the [two] stones'): the birth-stool / midwife's seat — a specific piece of equipment. Render with the descriptive English.
Saadia's word for the obscure 'פרך' (rigor/harsh labor) — 'iqmā' = abasement, breaking-down of dignity. Render as 'with cruelty' or 'with harshness'.

entries.en: guards of tribute / wardens of corvée
entries.note: Saadia's interpretation of שרי מסים: officers entrusted with collecting forced labor/tribute. Captures both the supervisory and extractive functions.
Saadia's gloss on the Hebrew ערי מסכנות — towns specifically for storage of grain/provisions (state granaries).
Saadia identifies the biblical Pithom with the al-Faiyum region in Egypt. Render with the parenthetical on first occurrence in a chapter: 'al-Faiyum (Pithom)'.
Saadia identifies Raamses with Ein Shams (= Heliopolis, ʿAyn Shams in modern Cairo). Render 'Ein Shams (Raamses)' on first occurrence.

entries.en: service / their hard service / pressed into service
entries.note: Saadia uses כ'דמה (service) — distinct from 'slavery'. Render 'service' or 'labor'. For ויעבדו ... בפרך use 'pressed into service with cruelty'.

entries.en: labors of the open country / wilderness labors
entries.note: Saadia takes שדה in oppressive-labor contexts as the open desert/wilderness (vs. cultivated field) — captures the Egyptian forced-labor on hard land (brick-fields, irrigation works).

entries.en: the Eternal / the Eternal who never ceases
entries.note: Saadia's PHILOSOPHICAL rendering of אהיה אשר אהיה — God names Himself by His timeless eternity (אזליה), not by 'I will be what I will be'. The shortened 'אלאזלי' (the Eternal) becomes the operative divine self-naming for the rest of the burning-bush dialogue. Render as 'the Eternal' (capitalized) as a divine name.

entries.en: I appeared / He appeared / will appear
entries.note: Saadia's signature anti-anthropomorphic move for 'descending' or 'appearing'. CRITICAL: never render Saadia's תגלא as 'descended' — even when the Hebrew has ירד. Saadia substitutes appearing/self-manifestation. This is the same theological gesture as Bereshit's 'the light of God ascended' for ויעל אלהים.
entries.source: Shemot 3 v.8,16; B17 v.1 (Saadia for 'I appeared to Abram'); passim

entries.note: Saadia's anti-anthropomorphic substitute for 'face of God / God [himself]' in contexts of beholding. Moses doesn't avert from God's face — he averts from God's LIGHT. This is the same principle as 'the light of God ascended' for the visible divine departure in Genesis. The light is the visible/perceptible mode of God's presence.
entries.source: Shemot 3 v.6; passim through the divine-encounter passages

entries.en: the angel of God / the messenger of God
entries.note: Saadia uses מלך (= the Aramaic מלאך, with א elided) for the divine messenger. The standard biblical 'angel of the Lord' construction. Render as 'the angel of God' (preserves the divine attribution).
Saadia's word for the Egyptian נגשים (the corvée-officers who drove the Hebrew laborers). Strong term — 'jalāwiza' connotes brutal enforcers.

entries.en: my plagues / my afflictions / a plague
entries.note: Saadia's word for the divine plagues. Distinct from אעגובאת (= wonders/marvels — the signs that prove divine action). Together: 'my plagues / my wonders' renders the doubled Hebrew נגעים + נפלאות.

entries.en: His decree has come to us / will meet you / will befall
entries.note: Saadia's standard rendering for the Hebrew נקרה/יקרא in encounter contexts: God's command/decree 'overtakes' or 'meets' the people. The verb ואפי (to come up to, to meet) preserves the sense of an unmissable divine summons.

Saadia's striking interpretation of the unusual Hebrew ונצלתם at Ex 3:22 / 12:36 — NOT 'you shall save/rescue' (the standard sense of נצל) but 'you shall divest/strip [the Egyptians]'. Captures the asset-transfer dimension of the exodus.

Saadia's word for the Hebrew שאלה in Ex 3:22 / 11:2 / 12:35 — NOT 'borrow/ask back' but 'ask as a gift / petition for gift-receipt'. Resolves the longstanding moral question of whether Israelites 'borrowed' from Egyptians never intending to return.

entries.en: the edge of the wilderness / the far side of the desert

entries.note: Cairo recension transliterates the Hebrew סנה as אלסנא. Some Saadia traditions use אלעוסג' (boxthorn/lyceum). Render 'the thornbush' either way.

entries.en: sent me / I have sent you / I will send

entries.note: Saadia's standard for לעולם (per Blau 3:22 in genesis-notes).

entries.en: generation upon generation / unto generation upon generation
the elders of the sons of Israel / the elders
the wonders / the miraculous signs / a wonder
entries.note: Saadia's word for divine signs given to a prophet as proof. Distinct from אעגובאת (wonders Israel sees, plagues on Egypt) and אלבראהין (proofs/demonstrations given to a prophet to perform).
Saadia uses אלבראהין (proofs) for המפתים (wondrous signs) — emphasizes the evidential function: Moses' staff-signs PROVE his commission.

entries.he_source: אלהים (Ex 4:16 'to be to him as God')
entries.note: MAJOR Saadia anti-anthropomorphic move at Ex 4:16: when Hebrew says Moses is to Aaron 'as אלהים', Saadia REFUSES to use 'god' (even in a comparative/representational sense). Substitutes אסתאד = 'master/teacher'. Same principle as 'I appeared' for 'I descended'.

entries.en: a spokesman / a translator / an interpreter
entries.note: Saadia for 'to be your mouth' (Ex 4:16): Aaron will be Moses' translator/spokesman — the one who articulates Moses' will to the people. Captures both the speech-mediation and authority-relay functions.

Saadia RATIONALIZES away the disease (Hebrew מצרעת = leprous). Renders simply 'white' — the visible phenomenon, not the medical condition. Applies the same de-medicalizing principle elsewhere in the Bible.

entries.ja: ד'ו נטק / ליס אנא ד'ו נטק
entries.ar: ذو نطق / ليس أنا ذو نطق
entries.en: a man of speech / I am not a man of speech
heavy of mouth and of tongue
the mute / the deaf / the seeing / the blind

entries.ja: פאשתד וגד אללה עליה / אשתד וגד אללה
entries.he_source: ויחר אף יהוה ב- / חרון אף
entries.en: And God was greatly angered with / And God's intense displeasure
entries.note: Saadia's standard anti-anthropomorphic rendering of 'God's nose burned' (חרה אף). No literal anatomy — just 'great anger / intense displeasure'.

entries.ja: צייר אלכלאם פי פאה / וצייר אלכלאם פי פיהם
entries.en: set the words in his mouth
I shall direct you / instruct you
send by whomever You will send
entries.note: Saadia's smooth gloss on the difficult Hebrew ביד-תשלח: 'send via whomever you wish to send' (i.e., send someone else).

Saadia takes חתן (bridegroom) in Ex 4:25-26 as referring to the SON Eliezer (the newborn), not Moses — interpreting the danger as falling on the uncircumcised child. Resolves the major exegetical crux of this passage.
Saadia interprets the cryptic 'ויפגשהו יהוה' as the angel suddenly attacking Moses' SON (the uncircumcised child), not Moses himself. Major exegetical decision.

entries.en: Thus says God, in honor / Thus says God in glorification
entries.note: Saadia ADDS משרפא (= 'in honor/with elevation') to the prophetic-formula כה אמר יהוה when God speaks elevating Israel. Rare interpretive flourish — preserves when present.

entries.en: at the lodging-place / at the night-stop
the foreskin / the foreskin of her/his son
I shall harden his heart / God hardened his heart
entries.note: Saadia preserves the divine causation in heart-hardening passages (does NOT soften by attributing to Pharaoh alone). The verb שדד = 'fastened/strengthened'.

entries.en: and he threw it / throw it [down]
the serpent / it became a serpent

entries.note: Saadia uses כם (sleeve / bosom-pocket of a garment) for the Hebrew חיק.

Saadia uses ערפא (= the Arabic ʿurafāʾ, sub-officers/foremen) for the Hebrew שטרים. Distinct from גלאוזה (the Egyptian taskmasters): the ערפא are ISRAELITE foremen appointed to enforce labor quotas on their own people.
Saadia's word for the brick-making quotas. Connotes both 'tax-quota' and 'tribute due'.

entries.en: to mold bricks / mold the bricks
brought trial upon / dealt harshly with
you have ruined our condition / standing
entries.note: Saadia smooths the Hebrew idiom 'made our smell stink' (הבאשתם את ריחנו) into the literal 'ruined our condition' — preserves the social-standing sense without the olfactory metaphor.

entries.en: May God look upon you and judge
labor / their works / to your burdens
lest plague or sword come suddenly upon us
celebrate a festival to me / make pilgrimage to me
entries.note: Saadia uses the Arabic ḥajj-cognate for the Hebrew חג — captures the pilgrimage-festival sense.
